action.I01.label: Show the portable chronometer
action.I01.001: This is our design. Only it looks as if someone has been wearing it for decades.
action.I01.002: Someone has. I need its original calibration. In the future, someone is erasing everything that doesn’t match.
action.I01.003: Mira is with the device. But first the hand pump needs repairing. Here’s a slip for the leather and the rivets. Lída in the village hall will lend you a punch if you help her.
action.I01.004: I thought time travel would involve less leather and fewer rivets.
action.I01.005: It’s precisely thanks to them that it works.
action.I01.x01: Good afternoon, Mr Bielik. Sorry to disturb you. You ought to see this.
action.I01.x02: First we look, then we talk.
action.I01.x03: I don’t understand that yet. But a device lies less than a person, and this one says you’re telling the truth.
action.I01.x05: A pump? What has a pump got to do with time?
action.I01.x06: It cools the model in the hut. Until it draws water, the measuring room stays locked.
action.I01.x07: And bring the punch back to me afterwards. I’ll return it to Lída myself. She remembers things she’s lent better than Rudo remembers his lines.
action.I01.objective: Collect the cuff and rivets from Štefan in the workshop yard, and borrow a punch from Lída.
action.I01.journal: Collect the cuff and rivets from Štefan in the workshop yard, and borrow a punch from Lída.
action.I02.label: Collect the materials on Oto’s slip
action.I02.001: Pre-cut leather for a cuff and two rivets. Punch the marked places first, then rivet. I’ll keep the slip.
action.I02.002: A clear procedure. You haven’t got one like that for my whole day?
action.I02.003: For the whole day I’ve only got one: lunch at twelve.
action.I02.x01: Good afternoon. Mr Bielik sent me – here’s his slip.
action.I02.x02: Slip, signature, materials. In that order.
action.I02.x03: The signature is Oto’s. I’d know it in the dark.
action.I02.x04: And if I don’t manage it by lunch?
action.I02.x05: Then there’s a snack at three. That’s issued without a slip.
action.I02.journal: Štefan issued me the leather for the cuff and two rivets, as on Oto’s slip.
action.I03.label: Tighten the stage flat clamp
action.I03.001: All it needed was the screw on the clamp tightening. The flat holds.
action.I03.002: Thank you. Oto said you need to punch a cuff. Here’s the punch – Oto will give it back to me later.
action.I03.003: If only someone could tighten my memory too!
action.I03.004: I haven’t got the right spanner for that in my bag.
action.I03.x01: Pity. My first line holds; the rest wobble like that forest.
action.I03.x02: Rudo, you stick to your script. The forest is holding now.
action.I03.z01: That’s exactly what little Zuzka told me yesterday. That our forest was hanging by one screw.
action.I03.z02: She was right. One screw was all it took.
action.I03.z03: She’s right nearly always. It’s just that nobody will lend her a screwdriver.
action.I03.journal: The stage flat clamp is tightened. Lída lent me her punch.
action.I04.label: Punch the marked holes in the leather
action.I04.001: Two marks, two holes. Not one more.
action.I04.journal: I punched two holes in the leather for the cuff.
action.I05.label: Join the cuff with the rivets
action.I05.001: The rivets are in. The cuff is closed and the edge has stayed straight.
action.I05.objective: Fit the finished cuff to the hand pump outside the test hut behind the park.
action.I05.journal: Fit the finished cuff to the hand pump outside the test hut behind the park.
action.I06.label: Replace the hand pump’s cuff
action.I06.001: Old cuff out, new cuff in. A few strokes of the pump and the water is circulating again.
action.I06.002: Now Oto can open the measuring room.
action.I06.objective: Tell Oto in his workshop that the hand pump works again.
action.I06.journal: Tell Oto in his workshop that the hand pump works again.
action.I07.001: Excellent. Here’s the key to the measuring room. Leave the punch with me; I’ll return it to Lída.
action.I07.002: May I tell Mira who I am and where I’ve come from?
action.I07.003: Tell her what you’ve seen. We’ll piece the truth together between us.
action.I07.x01: The pump draws. The new cuff fits and nothing drips.
action.I07.x02: Show me your hands. Dry. Then it really doesn’t drip.
action.I07.x03: And if she asks me why I’m wearing such odd shoes?
action.I07.x04: Mira doesn’t look at shoes. She looks at what people do with their hands.
action.I07.objective: Unlock the door of the measuring room by the hand pump.
action.I07.journal: Unlock the door of the measuring room by the hand pump.
action.I08.label: Unlock the measuring room
action.I08.001: I expected a secret entrance to the past. It’s an ordinary door and an ordinary key.
action.I08.objective: Talk to twenty-two-year-old Mira in the measuring room.
action.I08.journal: Talk to twenty-two-year-old Mira in the measuring room.
action.I09.001: So, a write-back. If it throws away the original difference, in time it throws away whoever caused it too. That’s why we have the return buffer.
action.I09.002: So what has disappeared isn’t completely gone yet?
action.I09.003: Until the write is closed, it’s only set aside. The device has to be able to bring it back.
action.I09.004: Then I need proof of what the original rule said.
action.I09.005: Make an imprint of the plate. The paper is in the loft, and Vera in the park has a blunt stylus. And here’s a registration form: the post office will confirm the date, and we’ll file the copy.
action.I09.006: You just believe me, like that?
action.I09.007: I believe you’ve come to preserve things, not to overwrite them.
action.I09.008: Here’s a second signed sheet for the duplicate, too. The content has to be identical; we’ll check it together.
action.I09.x01: You’re the one who mended the pump? Oto said you’d come. Talk – I’ll carry on measuring.
action.I09.x02: Good afternoon. In the future, someone is erasing everything that doesn’t fit their model. And overwriting it retrospectively.
action.I09.x03: My gran would say the same. Well… a friend of mine.
action.I09.x04: Your friend has sense. Give her my regards.
action.I09.x05: So: paper from the loft, the stylus from Vera, and then the post office.
action.I09.x06: And don’t crumple the sheet. On a crumpled one the imprint would only be half legible.
action.I09.z01: Vera draws on a bench in the park. Little Zuzka plays hopscotch next to her.
action.I09.z02: The one playing hopscotch? I saw her on my way here.
action.I09.z03: That’s her. If you get lost in Ivanka, ask her. She can find her way anywhere here with her eyes closed.
action.I09.objective: Make a legible imprint of the plate, and have the registration form confirmed in duplicate at the post office.
action.I09.journal: Make a legible imprint of the plate, and have the registration form confirmed in duplicate at the post office.
action.I10.001: Mira sent me to you. I’m making an imprint of the calibration plate and I need something blunt.
action.I10.002: Then take my stylus. Press the paper down first, then trace round the edges. Don’t scratch into the plate.
action.I10.003: A stylus you mustn’t scratch with. I’ll remember that.
action.I10.004: That’s why it’s blunt. It remembers it for you.
action.I10.z01: Auntie Vera keeps the blunt one in her case. She keeps the sharp ones for herself.
action.I10.z02: Zuzka, you know my case better than I do.
action.I10.z03: Because I count the styluses. Five sharp ones and one blunt one.
action.I10.z04: And what else do you need?
action.I10.z05: I need one form twice. Both exactly the same.
action.I10.z06: Mr Baran at the post office has black paper for that. You write on top and it writes itself underneath.
action.I10.z07: Carbon paper. It’s at the post office by the counter, for anyone.
action.I10.z08: Thank you both. I’ll bring the stylus back afterwards.
action.I10.z09: Leave it with Mira afterwards – she’ll give it back to me. You’ll be doing enough walking round Ivanka as it is.
action.I10.journal: Vera lent me a blunt stylus. It mustn’t scratch the plate.
action.I11.label: Take the waxed sheet
action.I11.001: A clean waxed sheet. I have to get it to the plate flat, not crumpled.
action.I11.journal: I found a waxed sheet for the imprint in the loft.
action.I12.label: Press the sheet onto the plate
action.I12.001: I press the sheet onto the cold plate. All four fields have come through.
action.I12.002: The plate stays here, where it was made. You take the imprint.
action.I12.journal: The waxed sheet has an imprint of the plate on it, still faint.
action.I13.label: Trace the imprint with the blunt stylus
action.I13.001: Origin. Voice. Consent. Return. And below that: ‘Different data are not invalid data.’
action.I13.002: I know that sentence. Gran used to say it to me when I wanted to throw out a broken radio.
action.I13.journal: I traced the imprint with the blunt stylus. The four words and Mira’s rule are legible.
action.I14.label: Take carbon paper for the duplicate
action.I14.001: The carbon paper is by the counter, for all the forms. Please, help yourself.
action.I14.002: Thank you. I’ll take just one sheet and keep my hands clean.
action.I14.x01: One sheet of carbon paper. I’ll make a note: one item issued, for official use.
action.I14.x03: I record everything, if you please. Otherwise one day somebody would find that nothing was ever here.
action.I14.z01: Carefully, please. It stains fingers too. Little Zuzka traces round her hands with it here.
action.I14.z02: The little girl who plays hopscotch in the park?
action.I14.z03: That’s her. She comes in to look at the new stamps. By the time she’s looked at them all, she’s traced round both hands.
action.I14.journal: At the post office I took carbon paper for the duplicate.
action.I15.label: Make a duplicate of the registration form
action.I15.001: I put the carbon paper between the sheets and write out the text. Mira signed both in advance. I’ll compare them and throw the carbon away.
action.I15.journal: I have the registration form in duplicate, both copies signed by Mira.
action.I16.label: Have the registration form’s date confirmed
action.I16.001: Two copies, identical content. Reference number Z-17, today’s date, stamp.
action.I16.002: I need it to be clear, even in seventy-three years, that this piece of paper existed.
action.I16.003: I can’t guarantee delivery in seventy-three years. But the stamp will last.
action.I16.x01: Good afternoon. I need this form confirmed. I have it in duplicate.
action.I16.x02: Certainly. First I read it, then the stamp. Otherwise I’d be confirming cake recipes.
action.I16.x03: That’s all I need. I’ll see to the delivery myself.
action.I16.x04: And don’t fold it more often than you have to. Paper tears at the folds first.
action.I16.objective: Take the stamped registration form and the imprint to the metal archive box in the loft.
action.I16.journal: Take the stamped registration form and the imprint to the metal archive box in the loft.
action.I17.label: Put the registration form in the box
action.I17.001: I’ve made a clean archive copy from your imprint. We’ll attach the registration form to it and lock it in the box.
action.I17.002: I’m taking the imprint with me. I’ll still need it.
action.I17.003: Then I’ll add the storage number to it. The plate and the original stay here. Leave me the stylus; I’ll return it to Vera.
action.I17.005: I may forget the face. I won’t forget what we did together.
action.I17.x01: Thank Vera for me too. And Mr Baran.
action.I17.x02: I will. Ivanka will be talking about you for a long time anyway.
action.I17.x03: That’s more than I hoped for.
action.I17.objective: Go back to Grob in 2020 and show Mira the verified imprint through the window.
action.I17.journal: Go back to Grob in 2020 and show Mira the verified imprint through the window.
action.E01.label: Show the portable chronometer
action.E01.001: My grandad made that with Mrs Hrušková. But this one looks much older.
action.E01.003: Yes. Do you know me, mister?
action.E01.004: A bit. So far, mostly the grown-up one.
action.E01.005: I remember this gentleman from Ivanka. Since then I’ve got older, and he hasn’t.
action.E01.x01: Good afternoon. Hi. May I show you both something?
action.E01.x02: If it isn’t another notice about a work brigade, yes.
action.E01.x03: What grown-up one? I haven’t been grown up yet.
action.E01.x04: Tóno, fetch the gentleman a chair. This is going to be a longer conversation.
action.E01.x05: We’ve only got one. And I’m sitting on it.
action.E01.objective: Tell Tóno the truth and show him the photo of the school yard from 2020.
action.E01.journal: Tell Tóno the truth and show him the photo of the school yard from 2020.
action.E02.label: Tell the truth and show the 2020 photo
action.E02.001: I’m Adam, Mrs Hrušková’s grandson. I’ll be born in three years. I’ve come from 2020.
action.E02.002: So I’m actually older than you.
action.E02.003: If we count the normal way, yes.
action.E02.004: And is the school still standing?
action.E02.005: Look – the same window. Your swallow’s there too, only it’s metal now.
action.E02.006: I haven’t made a metal one yet. So I’ll make one some day, then.
action.E02.007: The photo checks out and I know the device. What do you need to preserve?
action.E02.008: One return bridge. If you store it the normal way, it’ll be lost by 2020.
action.E02.009: I’ll take care of the materials and making it. Here’s a signed slip for the store. We can hide a spare in the service cavity in the low wall.
action.E02.010: I’ll draw a map. And when we meet again some day, say: ‘The swallow comes back.’
action.E02.011: Deal. But you don’t have to stop living a normal life because of it.
action.E02.012: Don’t worry. We’ve got a test tomorrow anyway.
action.E02.k01: Take the slip to the store, to Mrs Marta Dobiášová. She’ll issue everything that’s written on it, and not a screw more.
action.E02.x01: From 2020? That’s even further than the year 2000. And that’s really far away.
action.E02.x02: And will it have the right centre of gravity?
action.E02.x03: It will. It hangs perfectly straight.
action.E02.x04: Lost? Things don’t get lost with me.
action.E02.x05: Not with you. But the school will move things and be rebuilt many times yet.
action.E02.x07: A history test. From now on I’ll take it more seriously.
action.E02.objective: Collect the parts on Oto’s slip from Marta at the store, assemble the bridge and hide it with Tóno.
action.E02.journal: Collect the parts on Oto’s slip from Marta at the store, assemble the bridge and hide it with Tóno.
action.E03.label: Collect the parts on Oto’s slip
action.E03.001: A requisition slip from Mr Bielik. A ceramic base and three copper links. It’s signed, so I’m issuing the materials.
action.E03.003: Give my regards to Tóno. He left a model aeroplane here the other day – he should come for it before it flies off.
action.E03.x01: Good afternoon. I have a requisition slip from Mr Bielik.
action.E03.x02: Let me see. Mr Bielik writes his slips so that even the night porter could read them without glasses.
action.E03.x03: When a slip is in order, it’s quick. And this one is. Here you are.
action.E03.x04: I’ll tell him. And if it does fly off?
action.E03.x05: Then I’ll record it as a loss. The first aeroplane in my inventory book.
action.E03.journal: Marta issued me a ceramic base and three copper links.
action.E04.label: Assemble the ceramic return bridge
action.E04.001: Following Oto’s drawing: three contacts, each a different shape. The board has no power; I’ll connect it and measure.
action.E04.002: Tóno has drawn a swallow on the label. Nobody will ever mix it up with another bridge.
action.E04.journal: I assembled a new ceramic return bridge on the service board. Its label has Tóno’s swallow on it.
action.E05.001: Would you have a jar with a seal? Mr Bielik needs to store a component for the school somewhere dry.
action.E05.002: Here’s a clean jar with a lid, and some dry wrapping paper. It isn’t new, but it’ll do the job.
action.E05.003: This one will last longer than you’d believe.
action.E05.x02: Good afternoon. I don’t know you, and I know everyone. What’ll it be?
action.E05.x03: The jar is returnable. Bring it back and you get your deposit.
action.E05.x05: I believe you. At home we’ve got a gherkin jar that’s older than I am.
action.E05.journal: Ružena gave me a clean jar with a lid and a seal.
action.E06.label: Put the bridge in the jar and seal it
action.E06.001: Dry packing, the bridge with the swallow label, the seal and the lid. I’ll tighten it twice.
action.E06.002: Now it needs hiding. Tóno will remember the spot longer than I will.
action.E06.journal: The bridge is sealed in a dry jar.
action.E07.001: You’re right, the cart has already caught it once. Here’s a ready-made guard. Put it up and I’ll draw the cart a detour.
action.E07.002: One day there could be some nice shade here.
action.E07.003: That’s why we’re planting it. But a lime that gets run over by a cart won’t give any shade.
action.E07.x01: Good afternoon. That young lime tree in the yard… the cart passes right next to it.
action.E07.x02: How long will it need a guard?
action.E07.x03: Until people learn to walk round it. On foot it takes them a few years; with a cart, longer.
action.E07.journal: Šimon gave me a guard for the young lime. When I put it up, he’ll draw the cart a detour.
action.E08.label: Hide the sealed bridge in the service cavity
action.E08.001: I’m putting the jar behind the service board. Second row from the top, third stone from the left.
action.E08.002: Here’s my map. I drew a swallow on it too.
action.E08.003: I’ll record it as a harmless technical reserve. Just don’t take it out every time you visit.
action.E08.004: I’ll remember the place. I promise.
action.E08.005: And I’ll try to come in the right year.
action.E08.x01: A nice map. Even a stranger could find it with that.
action.E08.x02: A stranger isn’t supposed to find it. That’s why there’s a swallow on it and not an arrow.
action.E08.x04: The one when we both need it.
action.E08.x05: And now the board back on and hands in your pockets. It’s December.
action.E08.objective: Put up a guard by the young lime and make sure the cart takes a different route from now on.
action.E08.journal: Put up a guard by the young lime and make sure the cart takes a different route from now on.
action.E09.label: Put the guard round the lime
action.E09.001: The guard is up round the little tree. From now on the cart will take the detour Šimon draws.
action.E09.002: A small thing. That’s exactly why I’m curious what it’ll become in a few decades.
action.E09.journal: There’s a guard round the young lime. The cart will go round it.
action.E10.001: I’ve written it down: lime with guard, the cart goes clear of the roots. And there’ll always be access to the low wall for servicing.
action.E10.002: So the next time they redo the yard, it won’t all disappear under tarmac.
action.E10.003: Once the lime grows up, people will look after this place even without my note.
action.E10.004: I’ll come and have a look. For me, it’ll be tomorrow.
action.E10.x01: Tomorrow it’ll still be a twig. Better come and look in a few decades.
action.E10.x03: Goodbye, then. And pull the store door to behind you, so I don’t get a draught.
action.E10.objective: In 1995, find Tóno at the school and tell him the agreed sentence.
action.E10.journal: In 1995, find Tóno at the school and tell him the agreed sentence.
action.Q6A.001: Béla stayed behind in the park. Put his feed in his bowl and he’ll come home. Štefan in the workshop yard has the mix.
action.Q6A.002: So I won’t be chasing the post round the park.
action.Q6A.003: That would be beneath the dignity of both you and the post.
action.Q6A.x01: And why doesn’t he come back by himself?
action.Q6A.x02: This morning I gave him ordinary grain. Béla is used to his own mix, and he knows how to make his feelings known.
action.Q6A.x03: Then I’ll bring him the right one.
action.Q6A.x04: I’d be most grateful. Without him the post office is far too quiet.
action.Q6A.journal: Alojz’s pigeon Béla stayed behind in the park. Štefan has the feed for him.
action.Q6B.001: For Alojz’s Béla? Here’s his mix. Just tip it into the bowl and step back, so he doesn’t take fright.
action.Q6B.002: Two steps and no slip. I can manage that.
action.Q6B.x01: Mr Baran says you have feed for his pigeon.
action.Q6B.x02: For Béla you don’t need a slip. He’s the only one I issue to on his word.
action.Q6B.x04: Because when he gets nothing, he sits on my hatch and stares. That works on me better than a slip.
action.Q6B.journal: Štefan gave me a handful of feed for Béla.
action.Q6C.label: Put the feed in the bowl
action.Q6C.001: The feed is in the bowl. I’ll step back so Béla can have some peace.
action.Q6C.002: He’s eaten, shaken himself and he’s flying straight to the post office. He knows the way home better than I do.
action.Q6C.journal: Béla ate the feed from the bowl and flew off to the post office.
action.Q6D.001: Béla is home, thanks to you. I’ll put a print of an old stamp in your notebook. As a keepsake – it isn’t officially valid.
action.Q6D.002: Thank you. My notebook is all numbers and arrows. This will be the first nice page.
action.Q6D.x01: And if you ever need to send a message, Béla will fly. Not far, but willingly.
action.Q6D.x02: He probably wouldn’t find my address.
action.Q6D.x03: Béla doesn’t find any address, if you please. He only flies home. That’s why he’s so reliable.
action.Q6D.journal: Béla is home. Alojz gave me a print of an old stamp in my notebook as a keepsake.
action.Q7A.001: Oh, the script! I lent it to Mira to rest her drawings on. And now I only know the first line by heart!
